rules.label: Financial Assistance Program - Charity Care
rules.quote: (III)The patient’s annual family income is NOT more than two hundred fifty percent (250%) of the federal poverty guidelines.

rules.label: Self-Pay Discount
rules.quote: a.All uninsured patients receive a 40% Self-Pay discount on their account balance at the time of billing.

notes: Policy references HDC guidelines for insured patient screening upon request only. Insured patients are not automatically screened; screening occurs only upon request per HDC guidelines.
Policy mentions that patients who do not qualify for financial assistance will be notified in writing by the Financial Counselor.

Patients with verified Medicaid out of state balances in which it is not feasible for AVRMC to complete an application with the out of state Medicaid intermediary will be considered indigent and all balances adjusted off as 'Charity'.
The policy states that if third-party coverage is discovered at a later date, any financial assistance write-off will be reversed, and third-party insurance will be filed.
The policy states that the application process is the same process required for applicants of CICP or HDC.

Policy states that a letter will be sent to each applicant informing him/her of the eligibility determination, the amount of financial assistance given, any remaining balances owed by the patient, and the payment plan, if any.
Policy states that patients denied Financial Assistance will be sent a letter informing them of the reason for denial.

Policy states that AVRMC Patient Accounting office will keep a log of financial assistance provided each fiscal year, along with all applications, of those approved and denied. Account notes will be maintained as well.
Policy states that in the event that third-party coverage is discovered at a later date, any financial assistance write-off will be reversed, and third-party insurance will be filed.
Policy states that all signed Opt Out Forms will be scanned into Meditech and maintained as a part of the patient’s record.

Policy states that for patient’s that are discharged or leave the facility without opting to be screened or signing the Opt Out form (verbal decline is not valid for opting out), AVRMC will contact the patient, or guardian, using their preferred method of contact, if known (phone call, text, email, etc.). AVRMC will attempt to resolve the patient’s desire regarding financial aid screening, apply or opt out, at least once a month for six months after the patient’s discharge or until the patient’s resolve regarding financial aid is clear.
Policy states that all communications with the patient must be documented, signed by the person communicating with the patient and maintained in the patient’s record.

Policy states that if the patient request that the hospital cease contacting them related to the screening for financial aid, AVRMC will document the patient’s request including the communicator’s signature and date and record the request as part of the patient’s record.

Policy states that if AVRMC has exhausted efforts to contact the patient and the patient does not respond in 182 days, AVRMC will consider the lack of cooperation as an informed decision to decline screening.

Policy states that patients that are screened for financial aid per the above guidelines and are approved (household income is proven to be less than 250% of the federal poverty level) shall have all outstanding amounts owed by the patient for the specific episode of care (may not apply to balances prior to September 1, 2022; to be determined by hospital management) adjusted off as ‘Charity’ and the patient will not be billed or collected from for such balances.

Policy states that nothing in this section limits or affects a hospital’s right to pursue the collection of personal injury, bodily injury, liability, uninsured, underinsured, medical payment rehabilitation, disability, homeowner’s, business owner’s, workers’ compensation, or fault-based insurance.

Policy states that billing patients who do not apply for or qualify for Financial Assistance: patients who do not apply for financial assistance or is determined to be ineligible for financial assistance, the 40% discount is the only discount that will be applied to the account balance.
Policy states that patients in this category will be subject to guidelines set forth in Section 5 below.

Policy states that AVRMC will not collect up-front payments from uninsured patients unless they have opted out of screening (signed the form). If an uninsured patient has opted out of screening for financial aid (signed the form) then the patient would be subject to AVRMC’s Co-Insurance and Payment Arrangement policy. Uninsured patients should still be given ‘good faith estimates’ of their cost for services received, but no request for payment should be made until the patient opts out (signs the form) or is not approved for assistance in another way (application rejection, request to not be contacted or lapse of notifications, 182 days).
